choices.content: It can take every real number in an interval
It cannot be represented by numbers
It takes only finitely many values or values that can be listed one by one

question.prompt: What characterizes the values of a discrete random variable?

solutions.explanation: A discrete random variable takes finitely many possible values or values that can be listed one by one. The number rolled on a die and the number of defective items are both discrete: their values can be listed this way. A variable taking every real value in a nondegenerate interval does not have this property. Therefore the correct choice is D.
solutions.title: Use the defining value-set property
